title: Kestrel escalation - postmortem follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the 2026-03-01 incident: RCA review, immediate mitigations deployed, proposed reliability improvements, and alignment on next steps and timelines.
topics: Longer-term reliability improvements (autoscaling, KV cache fixes)
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the postmortem for last Monday's outage and make sure next steps are clear. Maya, thanks for taking time.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Thanks, yeah appreciate it. We had a pretty bad customer-visible spike for about 18 minutes, service errors and timeouts.
[00:20] Daniel Cho: Just to frame it, our internal timeline shows the latency spike started at 09:07 UTC, concurrent GPU preemptions and a cache miss storm that caused the serving pool to overcommit.
[00:31] Liam O'Connor: Yup, we saw the same — KV cache churned, we had a fallback to cold starts and then autoscaler couldn't spin up at the expected rate. The retry traffic amplified the problem.
[00:44] Sophie Martinez: In the RCA doc we linked in chat we called out three contributing factors: preemptions on the spot pool, an edge case in cache eviction logic, and a throttling config that was too aggressive which blocked warm-up.
[01:05] Rosa Alvarez: From security perspective, our main ask is audit log retention and verification that logs are immutable; we saw some gaps in correlation across regions.
[01:20] Priya Nair: Quick note — we've attached the postmortem PDF and the benchmark spreadsheet, links in the meeting notes.
[01:28] Jonas Meyer: Quick Q: when you say preemptions, is that host-level or container-level? We need exact semantics for our compliance team.
[01:36] Daniel Cho: Good question — it's host-level preemption on the spot pool; the runtime will currently drain containers but KV state wasn't checkpointed before eviction in this path.
[01:50] Liam O'Connor: That explains the cache misses — we saw a TTL cascade.
[01:56] Sophie Martinez: Short term we pushed three mitigations: 1) turned on a reserve capacity floor for Kestrel's Dedicated pool to avoid spot-only placement; 2) patched cache eviction so it prefers LRU with priority pins for hot prefixes; 3) relaxed the throttling gate so warm-up can proceed. These went live at 11:30 UTC yesterday.
[02:22] Maya Patel: We validated — errors dropped, but we noticed a small regression in cost for the last 24h which we need to reconcile with Finance.
[02:32] Priya Nair: We'll provide a cost delta report for the reserve capacity — expected to be small but we'll quantify.
[02:40] Sophie Martinez: For longer term, the plan in the doc includes: persistent KV checkpoints to object-store every N minutes, an autoscaler warm pool, and regional fallback policies to avoid cascading retries.
[02:55] Jonas Meyer: Timeline?
[02:58] Daniel Cho: We estimate checkpoints + eviction fixes in 3 sprints (approx 6 weeks), warm pool/A1 in 2 sprints after that, regional fallback policy design parallelized with our on-call improvements.
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: From Kestrel side we'll want a pilot run — synthetic load testing against the checkpointed kernels before you flip it on in prod.
[03:24] Evan Reed: That's on our plan; propose a 2-week pilot in your staging region with the benchmark harness. We'll run the benchmarks and share results.
[03:33] Rosa Alvarez: Also need an update to the SOC2 artifact — the changes to checkpointing and autoscaling will touch controls. We'll need an engineer-level writeup for auditors.
[03:45] Sophie Martinez: We'll package a controls impact memo.
[03:48] Maya Patel: One other item — are there any mitigations for reducing RTO while autoscaler spins up? We saw 12 seconds to first usable instance and that led to retries stacking.
[03:59] Daniel Cho: We can add a warm standby pool and a fast warmup path that preloads KV hot prefixes into memory; that's part of the warm pool effort. Also tuning OS-level preemption handling to checkpoint quicker.
[04:18] Jonas Meyer: Competitor question — have you considered switching to more conservative placement on Vertex or Anthropic managed endpoints? Our procurement is asking.
[04:27] Sophie Martinez: We discussed alternatives; switching endpoints is non-trivial and would change latency/cost profiles. We think the targeted mitigations are lower risk. We'll document comparisons.
[04:40] Maya Patel: Ok, let's walk through the action items then.
[04:44] Sophie Martinez: Action item 1: Sophie to share full postmortem doc and the patched eviction code diff by Friday.
[04:51] Sophie Martinez: Action item 2: Daniel to schedule a pilot benchmark run with Kestrel (staging) and provide test plan by Wednesday.
[04:58] Sophie Martinez: Action item 3: Priya to deliver cost delta report for reserve capacity within 48 hours.
[05:05] Sophie Martinez: Action item 4: Evan to draft controls impact memo for SOC2 and share with Rosa by next Tuesday.
[05:12] Rosa Alvarez: We'll review and send any auditor questions.
[05:16] Liam O'Connor: We also want a single point of contact for incident follow-ups — can you assign an SRE?
[05:21] Sophie Martinez: Evan will be primary SRE contact, Daniel backup.
[05:25] Jonas Meyer: Quick nit — please embed the request/response traces for the 09:07-09:25 window in the postmortem. They were useful during triage.
[05:34] Daniel Cho: We'll attach traces and the sampling config.
[05:38] Maya Patel: Any concerns about data residency? Some of the warm pool nodes were in eu-west while traffic is us-east only. Need to ensure no PII leakage in checkpoints.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Checkpoint storage will be configurable to customer-managed S3 and KMS. We'll include residency controls in the design.
[05:58] Rosa Alvarez: Good, we need KMS key rotation notes too.
[06:02] Sophie Martinez: We'll include key rotation and HSM options.
[06:06] Maya Patel: Okay, thanks all. We'll expect the doc and pilot plan and then reconvene after pilot results.
[06:13] Sophie Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and calendar.
[06:17] (meeting ends)
